rule.title: Hermetic Test Isolation and Explicit Test Sizing
rule.statement: Tests must be explicitly categorized by size (Small/Unit, Medium/Integration, Large/E2E). Small tests must be hermetic, running in-memory with zero disk, network, or external process access.
rule.rationale: Non-hermetic unit tests that make network calls or rely on external state are flaky, slow down feedback loops, and fail intermittently in CI environments.
rule.implementation_guidance: Small tests execute in milliseconds. Medium tests use local database containers. Large tests run full browser workflows.

forbidden.example: A 'unit test' that makes real HTTP fetch calls to a live external API server.

preferred.example: Small test: pure math chunking test in Vitest (<10ms). Medium test: Supertest + test database (<500ms).

source.evidence_quote: Google classifies tests as Small, Medium, and Large. Small tests must be hermetic: no access to network or disk. Hermetic tests are fast, reliable, and deterministic.
